name: The ascent in yoga of BhG ch. 6

stages.name: ārurukṣu
stages.gloss: one wishing to ascend to yoga
stages.description: For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means (6.3); action done without depending on its fruit makes one renunciant and yogin (6.1).

stages.name: yogārūḍha
stages.gloss: one who has ascended to yoga
stages.description: When one is attached neither to sense objects nor to actions and has renounced all intentions, one has ascended to yoga; for him calm (śama) is the means (6.3–4).

stages.name: yuñjīta (constant practice of meditation)
stages.description: Constant meditation in solitude on a firm seat, one-pointed, the mind fixed on the Lord, with moderation in food and sleep; gradually stilling the mind and bringing it back when it wanders (6.10–17, 6.24–26).

stages.name: yukta
stages.description: When the restrained mind rests in the self alone, free of craving for all desires, one is called yoked; the mind is like a lamp in a windless place (6.18–19).

stages.name: yoga (duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyoga)
stages.description: The stilled mind comes to rest, the self is seen by the self, boundless happiness beyond the senses is known and one is unshaken by sorrow — the disconnection from union with suffering (6.20–23).

stages.name: brahmabhūta / brahma-saṃsparśa
stages.description: The highest happiness comes to the calmed, stainless yogin who has become Brahman; he attains the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman (6.27–28).

stages.name: sarvatra samadarśana
stages.description: Seeing the self in all beings and all beings in the self, seeing the Lord everywhere, abiding in him however one lives; seeing pleasure and pain everywhere by likeness to oneself (6.29–32).

stages.name: parā gati / nirvāṇa-paramā śānti
stages.gloss: the highest goal; peace culminating in nirvāṇa
stages.description: The yogin always yoking himself attains the peace culminating in nirvāṇa that abides in the Lord (6.15); striving, cleansed, perfected over many births, he reaches the highest goal (6.45).

notes: Extractor A's reading of chapter 6. Stages 1–2 are the text's own pair (6.3); stages 3–8 follow the chapter's order of description rather than an explicit numbered sequence. The chapter also says the ascent may span many births (6.41–45) and that of all yogins the faithful worshipper of the Lord is the most yoked (6.47). Bands are a tentative interpretive alignment (interpretation layer).
